entries.title: P0003: fixed-length source scope and unverified current status
entries.statement: Historical conjecture, current openness UNKNOWN: Grimmett Question 2.2 asks whether the uniform n-step self-avoiding walk on the honeycomb lattice, starting at the origin with free endpoint, converges weakly after a suitable rescaling to an SLE(8/3) random curve. The source does not specify rescaling, SLE geometry or stopping, parametrization, or topology. The critical-fugacity boundary-to-boundary chordal conjecture is a related formulation; equivalence to this fixed-length question is not established here.
entries.domain: probability; self-avoiding walk; discrete complex analysis

entries.title: Proposed honeycomb observable compactness bridge
entries.statement: Proposed observable compactness bridge (false for arbitrary complex midpoint fields): on honeycomb domains with mesh tending to zero, the vertex relation sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F(p)=0, a uniform sup bound, and a fixed full boundary trace would force a locally uniform continuous holomorphic subsequential limit. This proposed implication needs extra hypotheses excluding lattice cycle modes. Its failure does not refute SAW-to-SLE convergence.
entries.domain: probability; self-avoiding walk; discrete complex analysis

entries.title: Exact boundary solvability and cycle freedom of the honeycomb vertex relation
entries.statement: Let V be a finite honeycomb vertex set, E the edges with both endpoints in V, H the boundary mid-edges with exactly one endpoint in V, and c the number of components of (V,E). Prescribe complex g on H and b_v=sum_{h in H incident to v}(h-v)g(h). Arbitrary complex interior midpoint values F satisfying sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F(p)=0 exist iff sum_{v in C}b_v=0 on every component C. If solvable, their complex affine dimension is |E|-|V|+c. For a connected plane graph this equals the number of bounded faces. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
entries.proof_text: Orient internal edges e=(u,v), put d_e=v-u and J_e=d_e F(p_e)/2. The vertex equations become B J=-b, where B has +1 at the tail and -1 at the head and b is the prescribed boundary contribution. Each component has one row dependency. A spanning-tree incidence minor with a root row removed has determinant +/-1 by leaf elimination, so rank B=|V|-c. Its image consists precisely of vectors with zero sum on each component. This proves the compatibility condition and affine dimension |E|-|V|+c. Euler gives the bounded-face count in the connected plane case.
assumptions: Finite honeycomb graph; arbitrary complex midpoint fields
entries.domain: probability; self-avoiding walk; discrete complex analysis

entries.title: Six-edge boundary-preserving mode of the honeycomb vertex relation
entries.statement: On a honeycomb mesh of side length delta, choose a complete interior hexagonal face with counterclockwise vertices v_0,...,v_5. The complex midpoint field H((v_j+v_{j+1})/2)=delta/(v_{j+1}-v_j), with indices modulo 6 and H=0 elsewhere, satisfies every vertex relation sum_p(p-v)H(p)=0, has six support points of modulus 1, and vanishes at every boundary midpoint. Adding H to a solution preserves every boundary value. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
entries.proof_text: On a complete interior hexagon v_0,...,v_5, define H at side midpoints by delta/(v_{j+1}-v_j) and zero at all other midpoints. At v_j the outgoing contribution is delta/2 and the incoming contribution is -delta/2; the third is zero. Other vertices see zero. Since side lengths are delta, the six nonzero values have modulus one. Every prescribed boundary value is unchanged by adding H.
assumptions: Finite honeycomb graph; arbitrary complex midpoint fields
entries.domain: probability; self-avoiding walk; discrete complex analysis

entries.title: Bounded fixed-boundary honeycomb midpoint fields can fail compactness
entries.statement: There exist simply connected honeycomb patches tending to a fixed hexagonal domain, with mesh delta_n tending to zero, and arbitrary complex midpoint fields F_n with full boundary trace identically 1, sup norm at most 2, and sum_{p adjacent to v}(p-v)F_n(p)=0 at every vertex, but no subsequence converges locally uniformly to a continuous function near a fixed interior point. One may take F_n=1+H_delta_n on a central face; two midpoints at distance sqrt(3)delta_n/2 have value difference of modulus 1. These fields are not asserted to be SAW observables. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
entries.proof_text: The constant field 1 satisfies the vertex identity because the three displacement vectors sum to zero. Add the six-edge field H from the preceding lemma. Then F=1+H has full boundary trace 1 and sup norm at most 2. A face-side midpoint p and the midpoint q of the third edge at the same vertex have separation sqrt(3)delta/2 and value difference of modulus 1. Center the chosen face near a fixed interior point while delta tends to zero. Locally uniform convergence to any continuous f would make the difference at p,q tend to zero, a contradiction. This argument uses arbitrary complex fields; it does not say the actual SAW observable has these modes.
assumptions: Finite honeycomb graph; arbitrary complex midpoint fields
entries.domain: probability; self-avoiding walk; discrete complex analysis

entries.title: Minimal linear constraints for the honeycomb midpoint boundary kernel
entries.statement: For a connected finite plane honeycomb graph with f bounded faces and compatible prescribed boundary midpoint values, the homogeneous vertex-relation kernel has complex dimension f. Fewer than f additional complex linear conditions cannot determine interior midpoint values uniquely. Exactly f suffice: orient each internal edge, put J_e=(v-u)F(p_e)/2, and impose c_i^T J=0 on the real signed cycle vectors of the bounded faces. These constraints give a unique solution to the algebraic boundary problem; they are not claimed to hold for the actual SAW observable or to prove a scaling limit. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
entries.proof_text: The oriented boundaries of the f bounded faces give real cycle vectors c_i. They are independent: zero edge coefficients force neighboring face coefficients to agree, and exterior coefficient zero propagates through the connected dual. Their number f=|E|-|V|+1 equals dim ker B, so C=[c_i] spans the homogeneous kernel. If J=C a and C^T J=0 then C^T C a=0; positive definiteness gives a=0, including complex a. For an inhomogeneous solution J_0, use a=-(C^T C)^(-1)C^T J_0 to satisfy the extra conditions. Fewer than f linear constraints leave a nonzero kernel by rank-nullity. These are algebraic constraints, not conditions proved for the SAW path sum.
assumptions: Finite honeycomb graph; arbitrary complex midpoint fields
entries.domain: probability; self-avoiding walk; discrete complex analysis

relations.rationale: The six-edge face circulation is a nonzero element of the classified homogeneous boundary kernel.
Adding the explicitly proved six-edge field to the constant field gives the persistent unit oscillation.
The fields meet the proposed local equation, bound and full boundary trace, but have no continuous locally uniform subsequential limit.
Rank-nullity and the exact face count prove the necessary number of extra independent linear conditions.
A face-dimensional kernel explains why the boundary trace plus vertex relation leaves interior ambiguity.
The observable bridge is a related SAW-to-SLE route; no equivalence to the fixed-length free-endpoint target is asserted.
The new source-scope note identifies the original source of this exact existing P0003 concept; it does not certify present openness.
